title: meta-loop wedge: auto-resume in-flight PRD, evented refusals, one state-file owner
description: Three connected defects in the deterministic chain, found in the 2026-07-06 audit when CAM-118 wedged after a cam run restart. (1) Absorbing wedge state: prd.json in flight (stories passes:false) plus phase idle has NO auto-resume path. The sidecar boot does not detect it (src/commands/sidecar.ts:1834-1898 has no re-arm), the meta-loop is gated off by prdInFlight (src/supervisor/loop.ts:1762-1767), and handleBlockedCycleBoundary treats prd-present as cycle-in-flight and skips silently (src/commands/sidecar.ts:1204-1206). Only operator cam next recovers. Observed live: CAM-118 planned plus audited, wedged idle. (2) Unevented terminals and refusals: finishTerminal('blocked') never calls logEvent (src/supervisor/loop.ts:725-728); cycle-in-flight, merge-watch-present and phase-not-idle skips are silent; there is no meta-loop-refused or cycle-wedged event kind and no durable marker for an implement-blocked terminal (contrast .cam-ship-stalled.json). The two failure modes that produced the incident are exactly the two without events. (3) cam-loop.local.md has three uncoordinated owners: phase setters (sidecar.ts:587-654), clearActive which rewrites the file omitting phase so it collapses to idle (sidecar.ts:305-352 plus renderStateFile in src/commands/next.ts:106-110, same mechanism as CAM-191 lost phase:shipping), and the orchestrator pane wrapper which rm -f the file on orch exit (src/commands/run.ts:283), deleting a live cycle signal under the running sidecar (the trigger of this wedge). Minor rider: meta-loop dispatch has no pending-guard; mutex-busy resets phase to idle and the dispatcher re-fires every ~4.7s (approx 20 dispatched:true events for CAM-98 on 2026-07-06); add a pending-guard or throttle. Fix direction: (a) at sidecar boot and idle-tick, detect in-flight PRD with pending stories plus idle phase and re-arm implementing with cam next semantics, gated on the same drain preconditions; (b) emit events for every terminal and refusal path plus a durable blocked marker the orchestrator reads at boot; (c) make the state-file lifecycle single-owner: the wrapper must never delete a live cycle signal. Cross-refs: CAM-191 (clearActive phase-drop), CAM-192 (image-stale block that started the incident).
